subTitleDesc.sub_title: Influence of Thin-Film Deposition Parameters on Film Structure and Electrical Properties
subTitleDesc.sub_describe: This inquiry topic aims to explore how variations in thin-film deposition parameters—such as deposition power, chamber pressure, substrate temperature, and gas composition—affect the microstructure and material properties of thin films. Students will investigate differences in film thickness uniformity, grain size, intrinsic stress, surface roughness, and electrical characteristics (e.g., conductivity and resistivity) under different PVD, CVD, or ALD conditions. Through literature review and data interpretation, students will develop a clear understanding of the correlation between process parameters, film structure, and resulting material performance, deepening their insight into thin-film engineering for semiconductor devices, optoelectronic components, and sensing applications.

description.describe_ch: 這課程的目的是介紹光學薄膜沉積的方法、製程技術及其相關的應用。本課程從基礎原理、製作方法、離子源輔助蒸鍍及濺鍍技術、薄膜特性量測及其應用等由淺入深，提供光學薄膜製程技術的全面概念，並探討光學薄膜的應用。
description.describe_eh: This course will provide an overview of thin film deposition methods, PVD processes and applications. Essential course aspects, thin-film growth from the evaporation, and sputtering techniques are discussed and highlighted with "real" examples and applications. The graduated students will also learn how to test and characterize the related properties of thin films.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol: Students are expected to arrive on time for all scheduled classes as lateness disrupts the learning environment, making punctual attendance essential. Active participation in class discussions, group activities, and hands-on sessions is highly encouraged, as engagement enhances the learning experience for both the individual and peers. Respect for classmates, the instructor, and guest speakers is fundamental, including acknowledging diverse opinions and maintaining a courteous tone during discussions. Electronic devices should be kept on silent mode, and their use should be limited to class-related activities to minimize distractions. Proper preparation is necessary, meaning students should come to class with the required materials, readings, and completed assignments to contribute effectively to discussions. Appropriate attire is expected in a professional and respectful learning environment, and any specific safety guidelines for laboratory sessions must be followed. Communication should be structured, with students raising their hands to speak and being mindful of the time allocated for discussions and questions. Collaboration is encouraged, but individual contributions must be acknowledged while respecting different perspectives and contributing constructively to group activities. Upholding the highest standards of academic honesty is essential, and students should avoid plagiarism and unauthorized collaboration on assignments and assessments. Regular attendance is required, and students should notify the instructor in advance if they cannot attend a class. Participation is a key responsibility, and students should engage in discussions, contribute insights, and ask questions to deepen their understanding. Constructive feedback should be given to peers during group activities, and students should be open to receiving feedback for improvement. Lab safety protocols must be strictly followed, and any safety concerns should be reported to the instructor immediately. Course-related communication should take place through designated channels, and students must check emails, announcements, or online platforms regularly for updates. Office hours should be utilized for additional clarification or assistance, with scheduled appointments if necessary. Assignments and projects must be submitted on time, as late submissions may result in grade penalties. Finally, students should be mindful of diverse perspectives and backgrounds within the class, fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment.

gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno:
Academic Integrity Guidelines for Graduate Course: Thin Film Technology
Academic integrity is a fundamental pillar of the Thin Film Technology graduate course, fostering an environment of honesty, respect, and ethical conduct. This document delineates expectations for academic integrity in assessments, classroom interactions, and post-course professional conduct while outlining potential consequences for violations. Students must complete all individual assessments independently, and the use of unauthorized materials, external assistance, or any form of cheating is strictly prohibited. Plagiarism in written responses, including copying from external sources without proper citation, constitutes a breach of academic integrity. All submitted assignments and projects must be original unless collaboration is explicitly permitted. Proper attribution is required for any external sources used, and group projects should acknowledge all contributors, clearly identifying individual contributions.
Active participation in classroom discussions is encouraged, and students must express disagreements respectfully. Personal attacks or inappropriate conduct towards peers or instructors will not be tolerated. Intellectual property must be respected, and students should acknowledge and credit others’ ideas rather than presenting them as their own. Beyond the course, students are expected to maintain ethical standards in academic and professional endeavors, ensuring proper citation and crediting of sources in publications, presentations, and other scholarly outputs. Ethical collaboration is crucial, and students must adhere to research integrity by ensuring accuracy in data representation and avoiding fabrication or manipulation.
Violations of academic integrity may result in various consequences. First-time violations may receive a formal warning to reinforce academic integrity expectations. Significant infractions may lead to grade penalties on assignments or exams, affecting overall course performance. Repeated or severe violations may result in course failure, and serious breaches may be escalated to the university’s academic integrity committee, potentially resulting in suspension or expulsion. By adhering to these guidelines, students contribute to a culture of integrity, ensuring a fair and ethical learning environment.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
Academic Integrity Guidelines for Graduate Course: Thin Film Technology
Introduction: The Thin Film Technology course at the graduate level emphasizes the importance of academic integrity to foster a culture of honesty, respect, and ethical conduct. This document outlines the expectations regarding academic integrity throughout the course, covering assessments, classroom interactions, and post-course conduct.
Expectations During Assessments:
  1. Examinations and Quizzes:
    • Students are expected to complete individual assessments independently.
    • Any form of cheating, such as using unauthorized materials or communicating with others during exams, is strictly prohibited.
    • Plagiarism in written responses, including copying from external sources without proper citation, is a violation of academic integrity.
  2. Assignments and Projects:
    • All submitted work must be the student's original work unless collaboration is explicitly allowed.
    • Proper citation of sources is required for any external information used in assignments.
    • Collaborative work should be acknowledged, and individual contributions clearly identified.
Classroom Interaction and Discussions:
  1. Respectful Engagement:
    • Active participation in class discussions is encouraged.
    • Respectful disagreement is welcomed, but personal attacks or disrespectful behavior towards peers or the instructor will not be tolerated.
  2. Intellectual Property:
    • Acknowledge and respect the intellectual property of others during discussions.
    • Do not present others' ideas or work as your own without proper attribution.
Post-Course Conduct and Professionalism:
  1. Academic Honesty Beyond the Course:
    • Uphold academic integrity in all academic and professional activities beyond the course.
    • Properly credit sources in publications, presentations, or any other work that involves the use of external information.
  2. Collaboration and Research Ethics:
    • Collaborate ethically with peers and colleagues.
    • Adhere to ethical standards in research, ensuring proper credit for contributions and avoiding data fabrication or manipulation.
Possible Consequences of Violating Academic Integrity:
  1. Warning:
    • First-time violations may result in a warning, emphasizing the importance of academic integrity.
  2. Grade Penalty:
    • Substantial penalties may be applied to the assignment or exam in question, affecting the overall course grade.
  3. Course Failure:
    • Severe or repeated violations may lead to failure in the course.
  4. Academic Disciplinary Actions:
    • Repeated or severe violations may be reported to the university's academic integrity committee, leading to more significant consequences, including suspension or expulsion.

Provide positive feedback to your peers during collaborative activities and embrace constructive criticism with an open mind, using it as an opportunity for improvement. If you ever need assistance or have questions, don’t hesitate to reach out. Wishing you an enriching and enjoyable learning experience! 
Warm regards, Sheng Chun Hung.
